title: Smooth purity
statement:
In the purity conventions of [def-pur-conventions], work at the finite
coefficient stage $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes, in the domain of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth
separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$
[def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, on the
small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with the derived
operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the twists of
[def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Substituting the diagonal/DNC identification underlying
[thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] (constructed below on this full
finite-type domain) into the tensor formula of
[thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] gives the canonical isomorphism

$$
\gamma_{f,K}:Lf^*K(d)[2d]\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;Rf^!K
$$

specified by [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]. Its Tate twist, shift, and
trace normalization are fixed by the prescribed Kummer normalization;
the trace is the counit composite of [def-pur-smooth-trace]. The
identification is compatible with arbitrary base change within this
scheme domain, through the smooth pullback exchange of
[def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange], and with composition of smooth
separated morphisms. Separatedness and finite type have the meanings
collected in [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties].

proof.text:
Put $M=Lf^*K$ and $T=A_X(d)$ [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The full-domain theorem [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] supplies the specified $\Pi_f:\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}T[2d]$, without absolute separatedness of $X,Y$. The canonical tensor map $\theta_{f,K}:M\otimes_A^L\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^!K$ is invertible by [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness]. Apply [lem-pur-oriented-derived-tensor-transport] with parameter $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, $P(K)=Lf^*K$ and $H(K)=Rf^!K$. Its sign-free reassociation $a_M$, inverse orientation and tensor map give
$$\gamma_{f,K}=\theta_{f,K}\circ(1_M\otimes\Pi_f^{-1})\circ a_M.$$
This is the specified arrow order of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]; its inverse and naturality follow from the transport lemma. No new chart orientation is introduced.

source.place: Three-arrow composite: twist reassociation, inverse orientation and canonical tensor map; extraction of returned proof Steps 1 and 3.

proof.text: On the separated-base affine models, [lem-pur-diagonal-affine-trace-site-comparison] identifies the trace of this diagonal-defined map with ordered restricted Kummer integration and identifies its adjoint transpose on the two sites. It includes $t_q^ph_q^p=1$, rank zero, all $E,n$, and independence of the annihilating exponent. It is used only on its separated model domain. For general $f$, [def-pur-smooth-trace] fixes the trace as $\epsilon_{f,K}\circ Rf_!(\gamma_{f,K})$. The given $\Pi_f$, tensor map and sign-free reassociation therefore fix twist $d$, shift $2d$ and trace with that normalization; no further scalar is chosen.

source.place: Three-arrow composite: twist reassociation, inverse orientation and canonical tensor map; extraction of returned proof Steps 1 and 3.

proof.text: For a Cartesian square in the stated finite-type domain put $e=Lu^*\gamma_{f,K}$ and $e'=\gamma_{f',Lv^*K}$. If $b$ is the canonical pullback-and-twist source identification, [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange] gives $\operatorname{Ex}^{!,\mathrm{sm}}=e'\circ b\circ e^{-1}$. Cancelling $e^{-1}e$ gives $\operatorname{Ex}^{!,\mathrm{sm}}\circ e=e'\circ b$, precisely [thm-pur-smooth-base-change-coherence]. Its domain allows arbitrary $v$; no flatness, smoothness or etaleness of $v$ is required.

source.place: Statement, typed inverse-purity composite; thm-pur-smooth-base-change-coherence statement, commuting square

proof.text:
For $g:Y\to Z$ smooth separated of dimension $e$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$, apply [thm-pur-composition-coherence] to the same specified maps:
$$\gamma_{gf,K}=c_{g,f}^{-1}\circ\gamma_{f,Rg^!K}\circ Lf^*(\gamma_{g,K})(d)[2d].$$
Its source comparison is $L(gf)^*K(d+e)[2d+2e]$ and its exceptional compositor is $c_{g,f}:R(gf)^!\cong Rf^!Rg^!$. Thus the twists and even shifts add in exactly the required order.

mathlib_searches.query: Smooth purity for exceptional inverse image of etale sheaves with Tate twist and cohomological shift

Smooth purity: the canonical exceptional inverse image of a bounded constructible finite Tor complex along a smooth separated morphism is its derived pullback with Tate twist d and cohomological shift 2d, compatibly with base change and composition
